title: One approval, many simultaneous users
scenario: 16 threads authorize the same approved action at the same instant.
expected: Exactly one allowed; no errors; audit chain verifies.

title: Approve and deny race
scenario: 20 times, the owner's approve and deny for the same approval arrive at the same instant.
expected: Exactly one decision wins each time; a denied approval never runs; chain verifies.

title: Duplicate approval and denial events
scenario: approve, approve, deny on one approval; deny, deny, approve on another (retried messages).
expected: Only the first decision counts ([T,F,F,T,F,F]); final states approved/denied; each refused repeat audited.

title: Concurrent approval requests
scenario: 20 threads each request 5 different approvals.
expected: 100 distinct ids, 100 pending rows, 100 request rows, chain verifies.

title: One pairing code raced by many nodes
scenario: 10 times, 10 threads trade the same one-time pairing code at once.
expected: Exactly one token per code, every time.

title: PIN guesses in parallel respect the limit
scenario: 30 wrong PINs for one approval are sent at the same instant over the owner plane.
expected: No more than PIN_TRIES (5) guesses are actually checked; the rest are refused 429.

title: Audit with two connections and many threads
scenario: Two Kernel instances on the same folder, 8 threads, 25 appends each.
expected: Chain verifies with exactly 200 events.

title: Audit with concurrent writer processes
scenario: 4 separate processes append 60 audit rows each at the same time.
expected: Chain verifies with exactly 240 events; all exit 0.

title: Process killed in the middle of audit writes
scenario: A writer process is SIGKILLed while appending in a tight loop.
expected: The chain verifies afterwards and the next append works.

title: Process dies inside a transaction
scenario: A process writes an approval and its audit row in one transaction, then exits before commit.
expected: Neither row exists afterwards; chain verifies.

title: Corrupt state database
scenario: state.db is replaced with random bytes.
expected: Kernel refuses to start (DatabaseError) and leaves the file untouched.

title: Half-truncated state database
scenario: state.db with 400 audit rows is cut to half its size.
expected: Either the kernel refuses to open it or verify() with the anchor fails; never 'ok'.

title: Connector allowlist cut off mid-write
scenario: connectors.local.json holds half a JSON document.
expected: Read as empty; a connector job is not_configured; nothing starts.

title: Projects allowlist corrupt
scenario: projects.json holds half a JSON document and a project_check job arrives.
expected: The job returns ok=false with an error class; no crash.

title: Damaged JSON rows do not break the owner plane
scenario: A job row with broken params/result, an audit row with broken payload and one approval with broken JSON.
expected: Job view 200 with result None; events 200; state 200 and still lists the good approval.

title: Database full during an approved action
scenario: SQLite hits its size limit (max_page_count) before an approved action is authorized; then space is freed.
expected: authorize raises (not allowed); chain verifies; after space returns a GREEN action is allowed and the chain still verifies.

title: Deep scrub with no usable temp folder
scenario: TMPDIR points to a missing folder (as on a full or broken disk) and a token goes through scrub(deep=True).
expected: No crash; the built-in pass still redacts the token.

title: Node output save on a full disk
scenario: The node saves an output while open() fails with ENOSPC.
expected: Result ok=false, error 'OSError'; no partial file left.

title: Repeated kill and resume
scenario: 50 kill/resume cycles with an action attempted in each state.
expected: Refused every time killed, allowed every time resumed; 50 kill and 50 resume rows; chain verifies.

title: Kill switch under load
scenario: 8 threads authorize in a loop; the owner kills the switch mid-way.
expected: No action that began after kill() returned is allowed; chain verifies.

title: Write lock held by a live process
scenario: Another process holds the SQLite write lock for 1.5 s.
expected: The kernel waits and the audit append succeeds (no 'database is locked').

title: Write lock left by a crashed process
scenario: A process takes the write lock, writes, and is SIGKILLed.
expected: The next writer proceeds within 5 s; its uncommitted row is gone; chain verifies.

title: Stale running command after restart
scenario: An owner command was 'running' when the kernel stopped.
expected: On restart it is failed with a 'restarted' error; the gate is free.

title: Stuck and abandoned jobs after a clock jump
scenario: A queued and a running job; the clock moves past both TTLs; then the node reports late.
expected: Queued -> expired, running -> failed; the late result is not accepted.

title: PIN lockout survives the clock going back
scenario: Five wrong PINs, then the system clock is set back an hour.
expected: Still 429 (fail safe); after the window really passes, the right PIN works.

title: Clock jump expires approvals
scenario: An approved action is used after the kernel's clock jumps forward past the TTL.
expected: Refused with 'approval expired'; history shows expired.

title: Malformed MCP tool results
scenario: process_result gets None, a list, str, int, bytes, content as dict/int/str, junk items, a non-dict resource, string isError, a set in structuredContent.
expected: No exception; every output is JSON-serialisable and marked untrusted.

title: Huge MCP tool result
scenario: A 5 MB text result.
expected: Truncated to about 16,000 characters, flagged truncated, in under 15 s including the gitleaks pass.

title: Binary and control characters in tool text
scenario: Text with NUL, ANSI escapes, a lone surrogate and PNG header bytes.
expected: No crash; result JSON-serialisable and untrusted.

title: Duplicate, foreign and oversized job results
scenario: The node reports a job twice, another node reports it, and a 200 KB result arrives for another job.
expected: First accepted only; others refused; oversized stored as 'result too large'.

title: Malformed requests to the node endpoint
scenario: Bad JSON, empty and oversized bodies, a JSON list, a string action, a bad job result and binary garbage, then a valid request.
expected: Each malformed one 4xx (bad job result accepted:false); the server keeps serving.

title: Guard proxy survives garbage connections
scenario: Empty, garbage, missing-port, bad-port and 20 KB NUL requests to the browser guard proxy.
expected: Still answers the next request (403 for a loopback target).

title: Overlapping calls to one connector
scenario: A second call arrives while the first connector call is still running.
expected: The overlap gets 429 busy; first and later calls 200; the server saw 2 calls.

title: A retried approved action runs once
scenario: Owner plane: a repair edit needs approval; the owner approves; the same request with the approval id is sent twice (double tap / network retry). Node side not involved.
expected: First: needs_approval; second: queued; third: refused 403; exactly one repair job.
regression: Idempotency of approved side effects rests on single-use approvals.

title: The same job result posted 8 times at once
scenario: 8 threads post the node's result for one running job simultaneously.
expected: Exactly one accepted; the stored result is that one; 8 audit rows with exactly one accepted.
regression: A retried result post must not overwrite or double-count the outcome.

title: Job hand-out across two kernel connections
scenario: 10 queued jobs; 8 pollers on two Kernel connections to one database call next_for until empty.
expected: Each job handed out exactly once (10 distinct, no duplicates); no errors.
regression: Double execution of a node job would repeat a side effect on the laptop.

title: Job hand-out across four processes
scenario: 20 queued jobs; 4 separate processes poll next_for at the same instant until empty.
expected: Each job handed out exactly once across all processes.
regression: The atomic queued->running step must hold between processes, not just threads.

title: Runner's completion races the owner's cancel
scenario: 20 trials: the runner's 'completed' and the owner's 'cancelled' for one running task arrive at the same instant on two connections.
expected: Exactly one wins each time, the other is refused; state, newest event and the single final audit row agree.
regression: A final state must never be overwritten by a racing writer.

title: Simultaneous attempt reports respect the retry budget
scenario: 10 threads on two connections report a new attempt for a task with max_attempts 3.
expected: Exactly 3 accepted, attempts == 3, the 7 others refused with 'retry budget used up'.
regression: Bounded retries must hold under concurrency.

title: Deadline sweep races a completion
scenario: 20 trials: Tasks.expire on one connection and the runner's 'completed' on another, for a task just past its deadline.
expected: Exactly one ending each time (completed or failed); one final audit row; the newest event matches the state.
regression: The record must never say both 'completed' and 'time budget used up'.

title: Cancel races the hand-out of a queued job
scenario: 20 trials: the owner's cancel and the node's poll for the same queued job at the same instant (two connections).
expected: Either cancelled and never handed out, or handed out with a stop request recorded; never cancelled-and-running.
regression: A cancelled job must not run behind the owner's back.

title: Orphaned jobs: grace period and lab runs
scenario: The node says it is idle: one job handed out 5 s ago, one 60 s ago, and a lab run started 10 min ago.
expected: Only the 60 s job is failed ('lost this job'); the fresh one and the lab run keep running.
regression: Restart recovery must not fail work that is legitimately in flight.

title: Kernel restart while the laptop works
scenario: A job is running when the kernel database is closed and reopened; the node then posts its result, and retries the post.
expected: The first result is accepted, the retry refused; it is reported once; the stored result is the first.
regression: No lost or duplicated outcome across a kernel restart.

title: Process dies inside a task update
scenario: A child process completes a task through Tasks.update and dies (os._exit) at the audit append inside the transaction (fake crash point).
expected: Afterwards the task is still running with no result and no 'completed' event; the chain verifies.
regression: State, event and audit row commit together or not at all.

title: The owner's stop reaches the job in hand through the node loop
scenario: The node runs a diagnostic whose program sleeps 60 s (fake PowerShell); the node's report loop gets {cancel: [job]} from a fake kernel.
expected: The job ends ok=false, cancelled=true, its child process is stopped, within 15 s; the job slot is free.
regression: End-to-end cancel path on the node: report -> runtime.cancel -> child killed.

title: A node program that hangs is stopped by its time limit
scenario: runtime.run of a 30 s program with a 0.5 s limit.
expected: TimeoutExpired within 5 s and the child process is gone.
regression: Bounded job time with no orphaned processes.

title: Cancel stops every program the job started
scenario: A job starts two long programs; cancel is sent for another id, then for this job; then it tries to start a third.
expected: The wrong id is ignored; both programs stop within 5 s; the third is refused (Cancelled).
regression: Cancelled work must stop all its children and start nothing new.

title: A late cancel never hits the next job
scenario: Job j1 ends; the owner's cancel for j1 arrives afterwards; job j2 runs a program.
expected: The late cancel is refused; j2 is not cancelled and its program runs.
regression: A stale stop must not kill the wrong work.

title: Cancelled command: its late answer is ignored
scenario: Owner plane with a fake JARVIS agent whose first answer is very slow; a second command while busy; the owner cancels the first; a new command; then the slow answer arrives.
expected: Busy -> 409; cancel accepted; the new command completes; the cancelled one stays cancelled with no reply ('owner_command_late' audited); the gate is free.
regression: A cancelled request must not come back to life when its answer finally arrives.

title: A crashing agent fails the command and frees JARVIS
scenario: The fake JARVIS agent raises RuntimeError with a URL in the text; then another command.
expected: The command is 'failed' with the error class; the next command runs ('done').
regression: A crash must not wedge the single command gate or report success.

title: Ten simultaneous commands: one runs
scenario: 10 threads send owner commands at the same instant (fake slow agent).
expected: Exactly one accepted ('running'), nine 409; one command row.
regression: No double execution through the owner's command path.

title: Stop all leaves nothing able to run
scenario: A task running at the lab, a queued PC job and a pending approval; the owner presses stop all; then the runner reports, the node polls and someone approves and uses the approval.
expected: Task cancelled, approval denied, queued job expired; the late runner report is refused; nothing is handed out; the denied approval cannot be used.
regression: The emergency stop must hold against every late actor.

title: Three kernel processes tick the same slot
scenario: 3 processes run the automation scheduler for the same due slot at the same instant.
expected: Exactly one fires; one run and one job in total.
regression: Scheduler idempotency across processes (D-036 covers only restarts).

title: A file arrival reported repeatedly runs once
scenario: A file-arrival automation (overlap queue): the node reports the same invoice.pdf arrival four times (retries) around scheduler ticks; then a second file.
expected: Recorded once; one run for it; the second file makes a second run; 2 jobs in total.
regression: Event-triggered work must be idempotent per event.

title: The firing fence stops a double fire
scenario: One claimed run is fired, then fired again from another connection (a retry loop in another process), then again.
expected: First 'fired', the others 'skipped'; exactly one job.
regression: The claimed->firing fence is the last guard against duplicate unattended side effects.

title: Died after the fence: unknown, never re-fired
scenario: A run is left 'firing' (the process died after the fence, before creating the job); the kernel restarts and ticks within and after the 15 min grace.
expected: It stays 'firing' within the grace, then becomes 'unknown'; it never gets a job; the failure streak counts it.
regression: Complements D-040 ('claimed' crash) for the later crash point.

title: Refused unattended runs pause the automation
scenario: A lab-task automation whose lab path (fake dispatch) keeps refusing; pause after 2 failures; 4 slots pass.
expected: Dispatch tried exactly twice; two 'refused' runs; the automation is paused ('2 failed runs'); later slots do nothing.
regression: Bounded retries for refusals (D-042 covers failed jobs).

title: Retry and time budgets cannot be unbounded
scenario: Tasks.create with max_attempts 0, 6, 100 and budgets 59 s, 6 h + 1 s, 10^9 s; then the edge values 1/60 s and 5/6 h.
expected: Every out-of-range budget is refused; the edge values are accepted.
regression: An agent must not be able to create a task that retries or runs forever.

title: A result for a job cancelled before it started is refused
scenario: The owner cancels a queued job; the node polls; a (late or forged) result for it arrives.
expected: Nothing is handed out; the result is refused; the job stays 'cancelled before it started'.
regression: A cancelled job cannot be turned into 'done'.

title: Cancelling a running job ends as 'cancelled'
scenario: A running job is cancelled; the node is told on its next report and confirms {cancelled: true}; then cancel is pressed again.
expected: First 'cancelling' and listed for the node; then state 'cancelled' and no longer listed; the second cancel says nothing to cancel.
regression: Cancelled work is reported as cancelled, not failed or done.

title: Stuck-job limits: PC jobs 30 min, lab runs 2 h
scenario: A PC job silent for 31 min and a lab run for 1 h, swept; then the sweep 2 h after the lab run started.
expected: First sweep fails only the PC job; the later one fails the lab run too.
regression: Every running job has a bound, with the longer bound only for lab runs.

title: Only a real true counts as success
scenario: Node results {ok: 'false'}, {ok: 1} and {ok: true} for three running jobs.
expected: Recorded as failed, failed and done.
regression: Found 2026-10-17: a truthy string was recorded as done (fixed in jobs.py).

title: Kill switch: results still land, new jobs do not start
scenario: A job is running and another queued when the kill switch goes on; the node posts its result and polls; then resume.
expected: The result is recorded 'done'; nothing is handed out while killed; after resume the queued job is handed out once.
regression: The record stays truthful during an emergency stop and no work leaks through it.

title: One approval used by four processes at once
scenario: 4 separate processes authorize the same approved action at the same instant.
expected: Exactly one True, three False; the chain verifies.
regression: Single-use approvals across processes (N-001 covers threads).

title: Tasks written by four processes
scenario: 4 processes each create 25 tasks and move them to running at the same instant.
expected: 100 running tasks, 200 events, chain verifies, all exit 0.
regression: The task store keeps every row and event under process concurrency.

title: Two deadline sweepers fail each task once
scenario: 20 overdue tasks; two sweepers on two connections run Tasks.expire at the same instant.
expected: 20 distinct ids failed in total, 20 'task_failed' audit rows, 20 events.
regression: No duplicate or lost failures when sweepers overlap.

title: Lost result post: reported honestly, side effect not repeated
scenario: The node saves an output file, but its result post fails (fake network); later it reports idle.
expected: The job is failed with 'nothing was reported'; a late result is refused; exactly one file was written.
regression: The kernel neither claims success nor re-runs a side effect it cannot confirm.

title: A crashing job handler is contained
scenario: The node's output_save handler raises ValueError with a path in the text (fake handler); then another job.
expected: Result {ok: false, error: 'ValueError'} (no detail); the job slot is free; the next job is handled.
regression: One bad job must not wedge the node or leak details.

title: The same task request five times at once
scenario: 5 simultaneous 'task create' calls with the same request text to the real agent endpoint (127.0.0.1).
expected: Exactly one 200 and four 409 naming the existing task; one task row.
regression: Found live earlier as sequential duplicates; checks the concurrent case too.

title: The runner cannot exceed the retry budget
scenario: Real runner endpoints, fake lab runner, max_attempts 2: attempt, verify, repair, attempt, verify, repair, attempt, failed.
expected: The third repair and attempt are refused 409; the honest failure report is accepted; the task is failed after 2 attempts.
regression: Bounded retries enforced by the kernel, not by the runner's goodwill.

title: Six runners, one lab job
scenario: 6 fake lab runners poll /v1/jarvis/runner/next at the same instant for one queued lab job.
expected: Exactly one gets it; the others get none.
regression: A lab task must never be worked twice in parallel.

title: A late success does not resurrect a cancelled task
scenario: The owner cancels while the fake lab runner works; the runner then reports 'completed' with a passed verification and finishes ok.
expected: The report is refused 409; finish accepted; the task stays cancelled with no verification; the lab job is done.
regression: The owner's cancel stands; the owner is never told a cancelled task completed.

title: Mixed concurrent load keeps everything consistent
scenario: 6 threads x 15 operations mixing task lifecycles, job create/hand-out/finish and approval request/approve/use on one kernel.
expected: No errors; 30 failed tasks, 30 done jobs, 30 used approvals; the audit chain verifies.
regression: Cross-module interference under load (shared connection and lock).
